title: Manage security through the information-system lifecycle: concept decisions 2
teachingQuestion: Which lifecycle activity must create or validate this security decision or evidence artifact?
focalInsight: Traceability from stakeholder need through operation and disposal keeps security accountable across change.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Retirement Disposal
nodes.definition: Controlled removal of system use, access, data, keys, media, dependencies, contracts, and retained evidence.
nodes.detail: Controlled removal of system use, access, data, keys, media, dependencies, contracts, and retained evidence.
nodes.decision: Plan when service ends or changes so disposition and revocation are authorized and verifiable.
nodes.failureExample: A retired service leaves live credentials and customer backups accessible.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Retirement is a security transition, not an administrative afterthought.

nodes.label: Security Acceptance
nodes.definition: Accountable decision that security evidence, residual risk, and operational readiness meet agreed criteria.
nodes.detail: Accountable decision that security evidence, residual risk, and operational readiness meet agreed criteria.
nodes.decision: Make only after required tests, exceptions, owners, and risk decisions are documented.
nodes.failureExample: A sponsor accepts a system without knowing an unresolved high-risk exception.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Acceptance is an informed authorization, not a project milestone.
